facts.fact: On Friday night just before dark Hattie walks down to the ocean.
facts.anchor: On Friday night, just before dark, Hattie walks down to the ocean.

facts.fact: Hattie raises one hand in a small wave then drops it and goes back to the house.
facts.anchor: She raises one hand in a small wave, then drops it to her side and goes back to the house.

facts.fact: Tommy startles in the kitchen chair where he had nodded off when Hattie comes inside.
facts.anchor: Tommy startles in the kitchen chair where he’s nodded off when she comes inside.

facts.fact: After calling Dustin they have taken turns keeping watch but there has been no sign of him.
facts.anchor: After calling Dustin, they’ve taken turns keeping watch since the simplest way to get the upper hand would be for him to show up a day or two early, but there’s been no sign of him.

facts.fact: Hattie makes herself a sandwich hoping the sight of food will entice Tommy but he only stares at the floor.
facts.anchor: She makes herself a sandwich, hoping the sight of food will entice him, but he only sits staring at the floor.

facts.fact: Tommy asks Hattie whether if this works things could really be good again.
facts.anchor: If this works, do you really think things could be good again?

facts.fact: Tommy says one of the worst things is knowing what Dad thought of him at the end.
facts.anchor: One of the worst things is knowing what Dad thought of me at the end.

facts.fact: Hattie tells Tommy that before he passed their father said he loved him and nothing would change that because love abides only itself.
facts.anchor: he told me he loved you and nothing in the world would ever change that because love abides only itself.

facts.fact: The sound like tiny fingernails tapping against the glass turns out to be snow starting to fall.
